_README: BASELINE OF LINKS THAT RENDER UNDER THE 44px MOBILE TAP-TARGET FLOOR. This is a RATCHET, not an
allowlist. Recorded 2026-08-20 when the site-wide tap-target sweep in test/functional.spec.js was
first written. Until then NOTHING in this repo measured tap-target size at all - tasks/backlog.md
P6-50 said so outright - and the gap shipped a live conversion bug (P6-61).
EVERY NUMBER BELOW WAS MEASURED IN CHROMIUM AT 375x812, AFTER document.fonts.ready, not computed
from CSS. Both halves of that sentence were learned the hard way and both are load-bearing:
1. NOT COMPUTED FROM CSS. The first attempt at this gate parsed each page's CSS and computed
padding + border + line-box. It reported 61 broken pages where the browser found 5, because
`.hub-cta-row` is a flex container whose default `align-items: stretch` was quietly pulling the
short button up to its taller sibling's height. It was blind to `.hub-link`, `.blog-link`,
`.job-card-link`, the leaflet controls and 574 unclassed anchors at the same time. Do not
replace this with a static check; the full rationale is written out at the test.
2. AFTER FONTS LOAD. Inter loads late and fallback metrics are shorter, so a control near the
boundary reads short before the swap and fine after. 404.html's 'Back to Homepage' button
measured 43px pre-swap and 45px post-swap; it was never actually a defect, and it is not
listed here. Measuring before fonts settle also made the P6-61 proof run report 11 findings
on the first pass and 10 on the retry, from the same button.
P6-61 IS FIXED AND IS NOT LISTED HERE. `.btn-outline-white` measures at least 44px on all 69 pages
that use it, with its label centred.
KEYED BY CLASS, NOT BY PAGE, ON PURPOSE. Keying by page would fail CI every time a new city hub
legitimately reuses `.brand-pill`, which turns the gate into friction to be silenced rather than a
signal to act on. An element is exempt if ANY of its classes appears below, so listing `brand-pill`
also covers `brand-pill premium` and `cat-pill` also covers `cat-pill active`. THE TRADE-OFF,
ACCEPTED AND STATED: a class listed here spreading to more pages is NOT flagged. What IS flagged -
the reason the gate exists - is any short link whose classes are all absent from this list,
including a renamed or newly transposed one.
THE BASELINE MAY ONLY SHRINK. A class listed here that no longer measures under 44px on any page
FAILS the sweep with an instruction to remove it. That is what stops this file rotting into
permanent silence. Do NOT add a class here to make a failing run pass: a newly short tap target is
a bug in the page, not a number to record.
'(unclassed)' is the bucket for short links carrying no class at all. It is deliberately coarse and
it is the least satisfying entry in this file: measured, it mixes footer contact links (the phone
and email lines render 15px tall, a genuine and fairly serious tap target) with breadcrumb 'Home'
links, which P6-50 already rules exempt as inline prose even though they do not compute as
`display: inline` and so are not caught by the sweep's WCAG 2.5.8 exemption. Splitting that bucket
needs a judgement pass over ~574 elements and is tracked in P6-62, not done here.
measuredWith: Chromium 375x812, after document.fonts.ready, via the test/functional.spec.js tap-target sweep
